name: Loma Linda University Health

ahrq.src: AHRQ Compendium of U.S. Health Systems, 2023, matched to CMS's hospital list (the site's June 2026 pull)

hc.src: Medicare hospital cost reports (CMS HCRIS, Worksheet S-3), fiscal year 2024 file

subs: Beds on its Medicare cost report. A licensed bed count usually runs higher.
Every intensive and special care unit counts: adult, cardiac, surgical, burn, neonatal and pediatric.
Each inpatient stay that ended counts once, whoever paid for it.
All inpatient days divided by discharges. Answer in days, like 4.5.
Patient days divided by the bed days it had available.
Medicare Advantage plans included. Counted in days spent in a bed, not in people.
Medicaid managed care plans included. Counted in days spent in a bed, not in people.
Two half-time employees count as one. Hospital payroll only: not clinics, not contract staff.
Interns and residents: doctors training after medical school. Two half-time count as one.
From AHRQ's 2023 list of who owns which hospital, matched to Medicare's hospital list.
Every one of its hospitals' latest Medicare cost report, added up.
Biggest by beds on its cost report. The answer names the hospital.
Two half-time employees count as one. Hospital payrolls only: clinics, offices and any health plan are left out.

questions.q: How many full-time-equivalent employees did Loma Linda University Medical Center have on its payroll in fiscal 2025?
questions.why: No other Loma Linda University Health hospital reports more; Loma Linda University Children's Hospital is next at 1,990. About 14.3 for every bed.

questions.q: How many full-time-equivalent employees did Loma Linda University Medical Center-Murrieta have on its payroll in fiscal 2025?
questions.why: That is the fewest of 3 Loma Linda University Health hospitals; Loma Linda University Medical Center has the most, 6,231. About 10.5 for every bed.

questions.q: How many full-time-equivalent employees did Loma Linda University Children's Hospital have on its payroll in fiscal 2025?
questions.why: That ranks second of 3 Loma Linda University Health hospitals; Loma Linda University Medical Center has the most, 6,231. About 5.5 for every bed.

questions.q: What percent of Loma Linda University Medical Center's inpatient days in fiscal 2025 were for Medicare patients?
questions.why: Traditional Medicare was 20 percent and Medicare Advantage plans 23 percent.

questions.q: What percent of Loma Linda University Medical Center-Murrieta's inpatient days in fiscal 2025 were for Medicare patients?
questions.why: Traditional Medicare was 22 percent and Medicare Advantage plans 32 percent.

questions.q: What percent of Loma Linda University Medical Center's inpatient days in fiscal 2025 were for Medicaid patients?
questions.why: That ranks second of 3 Loma Linda University Health hospitals; Loma Linda University Children's Hospital runs highest, 69 percent. Traditional Medicaid was 6 percent and Medicaid managed care plans 37 percent.

questions.q: What percent of Loma Linda University Medical Center-Murrieta's inpatient days in fiscal 2025 were for Medicaid patients?
questions.why: That is the lowest of 3 Loma Linda University Health hospitals; Loma Linda University Children's Hospital runs highest, 69 percent. Traditional Medicaid was 3 percent and Medicaid managed care plans 25 percent.

questions.q: What percent of Loma Linda University Children's Hospital's inpatient days in fiscal 2025 were for Medicaid patients?
questions.why: No other Loma Linda University Health hospital runs higher; Loma Linda University Medical Center is next at 43 percent. Traditional Medicaid was 46 percent and Medicaid managed care plans 23 percent.

questions.q: Across all of Loma Linda University Health's hospitals, what percent of inpatient days were for Medicare patients?
questions.why: Across every U.S. hospital's cost report it is 44 percent.

questions.q: Across all of Loma Linda University Health's hospitals, what percent of inpatient days were for Medicaid patients?
questions.why: Across every U.S. hospital's cost report it is 24 percent.

questions.why: No other Loma Linda University Health hospital kept patients longer; Loma Linda University Children's Hospital is next at 7.4 days. Across the cost reports of U.S. general hospitals it averages 5.0 days.

questions.q: On an average day in fiscal 2025, what percent of Loma Linda University Children's Hospital's beds had a patient in them?
questions.why: Patient days divided by the bed days it had available.

questions.q: How many hospitals does Loma Linda University Health run, by the federal list of health systems?
questions.why: All of them are in California. A system's own count can differ: it may count campuses on their own, or hospitals that joined after 2023.

questions.q: How many beds do Loma Linda University Health's hospitals report to Medicare, added together?
questions.why: From all 3 hospitals' latest cost reports, mostly 2025.

questions.q: How many intensive care beds do Loma Linda University Health's hospitals report to Medicare, added together?
questions.why: That is 39 percent of their 912 beds. From all 3 hospitals' latest cost reports, mostly 2025.

questions.why: About 116 a day. From all 3 hospitals' latest cost reports, mostly 2025.
